messages:
maria: seeing a 200-400ms tail on a handful of 32k-context requests around 11:40 UTC. p50 fine, p99 spikes. anyone else?
tim: yep spotted it on canary. correlates with a KV pager churn metric rising.
raj: logs show repeated evict->reinsert cycles, looks like hotset thrashing.
maria: weird part: eviction_policy is LRU on that pool, but the profiler shows eviction batches flipping to FIFO under high pressure?
sophia: could be the fast-path preemptive throttle kicking in and rewriting the policy for fairness. we added that last month for bursted allocs.
lee: @sophia do we have telemetry that marks when the policy transitions? perf-bot should emit an event.
perf-bot: metric:event kv_eviction_policy_switch { pool: gpu-pool-5, from: LRU, to: FIFO, time: 2026-03-17T11:40:12Z }
tim: here are relevant samples from perf (snip):
```
kv_evict: 72% cpu (reclaim loop)
kv_reinsert: 18% cpu (memcopy + slot touch)
page_faults/hr: +1200
latency_tail_jump: +320ms
```
raj: batching heuristics might interact: when batching aggregates many long contexts, KV cache insert patterns change and we end up with long-lived entries being deprioritized by LRU incorrectly.
maria: hypothesis: policy switch -> FIFO handshake -> reinsert storms -> pager gains -> latency spike. need repro and fix.
sophia: quick mitigation: disable dynamic policy switching in that pool, enforce sticky LRU, and tighten preemption window. can we flip for an hour?
lee: +1 to rollback. I'll patch a hot config flag and rollout to canary now.
perf-bot: deploy:start rollout/e-vict-policy-hotfix -> canary
tim: also adding a lightweight trace in kernel selection path to log chosen eviction strategy and batching window, so we can correlate next occurrence. small inline patch:
```json
{"trace_eviction_policy": true, "batch_window_ms": 8}
```
raj: also capture KV reuse ratio histogram, that will show if reinsert churn is killing reuse.
maria: ok roll forward with canary, i'll run the long-context perf suite against it. will report back in 30m. :thumbsup:
